# lvlath/go

> lvlath/go is a deterministic, contract-driven, pure-Go library for graph modeling, traversal, shortest paths, spanning trees, network flow, routing, dense matrix computation, combinatorial optimization, grid construction, reproducible fixtures, and time-series alignment.


Maintained repository: `github.com/lvlath/go`.
Use `go get github.com/lvlath/go`; read `go.mod` for the required Go version.
The maintained implementation requires Go 1.23.4 or newer and is licensed under `AGPL-3.0-only`.

Canonical Go module: `github.com/lvlath/go`

Install with:

```bash
go get github.com/lvlath/go@latest
```


## Start here

- [Repository README](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/README.md): Overview and working entry points.
- [Go module](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lvlath/go/main/go.mod): Module path and Go requirement.
- [Tutorial](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/lvlath/go/main/docs/TUTORIAL.md): Package selection and composition.
- [Go reference](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go): Published API documentation; check the selected version.

## Important usage rules:

- Treat package documentation and the current `pkg.go.dev` API as authoritative. Do not invent exported functions, options, fields, or result methods.
- Build graph topology with `core.Graph`; use algorithm packages for computation and `matrix` for dense numeric artifacts.
- Deterministic ordering and tie-breaking are observable API behavior where documented.
- Public sentinel errors are checked with `errors.Is`; never match error strings.
- Non-trivial algorithms return inspectable evidence such as paths, predecessor maps, cycle witnesses, trees, cuts, residual graphs, tours, alignments, or matrices.
- Numeric meanings are package-specific. Do not treat `0`, `+Inf`, `NaN`, a missing edge, an unreachable state, and an untracked witness as interchangeable.
- Preserve caller ownership and aliasing rules documented by each package. Do not mutate returned or retained values unless the API explicitly permits it.
- Prefer explicit options over inferred policy. Never silently substitute a weaker algorithm, memory mode, matching policy, topology interpretation, or numeric encoding.

## Package-selection guide:

- Use `core` for deterministic, thread-safe graph topology and explicit directed/weighted/loop/multi-edge/mixed-edge capabilities.
- Use `builder` for deterministic fixtures and reproducible graph construction.
- Use `bfs` for unweighted shortest-hop traversal, paths, layers, and weak components.
- Use `dfs` for depth-first forests, finish order, cycle witnesses, and topological sorting.
- Use `dijkstra` for non-negative weighted single-source shortest paths.
- Use `mst` for minimum spanning trees or explicitly requested spanning forests.
- Use `flow` for max-flow/min-cut computation and residual-network evidence.
- Use `gridgraph` to generate lattice graphs for routing and traversal workloads.
- Use `matrix` for dense matrices, graph adapters, metric closure, algebra, statistics, and factorization workflows.
- Use `tsp` for exact, approximate, heuristic, and local-search tour construction under documented assumptions.
- Use `dtw` for deterministic scalar, multivariate, or cost-matrix dynamic time warping.

## Critical semantic boundaries:

- `bfs`: discovery/visited state is not the same as processing order.
- `dfs`: discovery order is not finish order and is not automatically a topological order.
- `dijkstra`: unknown target, known unreachable target, disabled path tracking, and missing path evidence are distinct states.
- `mst`: a disconnected graph has no single spanning tree; forest behavior must be requested explicitly.
- `flow`: a scalar maximum-flow value is incomplete when the caller needs residual or cut evidence.
- `matrix`: classic adjacency may use `0` for absence; zero-preserving weighted adjacency uses finite `0` for a real zero-weight edge and `+Inf` for absence. All-zero weighted graphs require explicit zero-weight preservation.
- `matrix`: metric closure stores derived all-pairs distances and must not be exported as if those distances were literal graph edges.
- `tsp`: exactness, metric assumptions, matching policy, time limits, and incumbent optimality are explicit contracts.
- `dtw`: alignment cost and recovered alignment path are different result products; path recovery depends on memory policy.

## Package documentation:

- [core](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/core): Deterministic graph topology, capabilities, identity, ownership, and concurrency rules.
- [builder](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/builder): Deterministic graph builders and reproducible fixtures.
- [bfs](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/bfs): Breadth-first traversal, shortest-hop paths, layers, components, filters, hooks, and partial results.
- [dfs](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/dfs): Depth-first traversal, finish order, cycle witnesses, and topological sorting.
- [dijkstra](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/dijkstra): Non-negative weighted shortest paths, path witnesses, cutoffs, and unreachable-state publication.
- [mst](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/mst): Prim/Kruskal minimum spanning trees and explicit forest behavior.
- [flow](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/flow): Ford-Fulkerson, Edmonds-Karp, Dinic, residual graphs, and cut evidence.
- [gridgraph](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/gridgraph): Deterministic two-dimensional lattice graph generation.
- [matrix](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/matrix): Dense matrices, graph adapters, zero-weight policy, metric closure, algebra, statistics, and factorizations.
- [tsp](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/tsp): Exact, approximate, heuristic, and local-search tours with explicit assumptions and stopping policy.
- [dtw](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/lvlath/go/dtw): Dynamic time warping, windows, slope penalties, memory modes, costs, and optional path recovery.

## Detailed guides:

- [Core guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/CORE.md): Graph contracts, topology, identity, ownership, concurrency, and operational examples.
- [BFS guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/BFS.md): Queue semantics, discovery versus processing, paths, components, and pitfalls.
- [DFS guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/DFS.md): Discovery/finish semantics, cycles, DAG validation, and topological ordering.
- [Dijkstra guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/DIJKSTRA.md): Input domain, unreachable states, witnesses, policy, and complexity.
- [MST guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/MST.md): Prim/Kruskal, strict tree versus forest behavior, and disconnected inputs.
- [Flow guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/FLOW.md): Augmenting paths, residual networks, cuts, and algorithm selection.
- [Matrix guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/MATRICES.md): Dense storage, numeric policy, zero-weight preservation, graph adapters, APSP, statistics, and factorizations.
- [TSP guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/TSP.md): Exactness, approximation assumptions, local search, limits, and result interpretation.
- [DTW guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/DTW.md): Alignment cost, path recovery, windows, penalties, and memory modes.
- [Grid graph guide](https://github.com/lvlath/go/blob/main/docs/GRID_GRAPH.md): Lattice construction, connectivity, obstacles, and routing scenarios.
